title: What If You Could Hear What People Really Think of You?

meta.topic: what people really think of you

scenes.narration: What if, for one day, you could hear exactly what everyone really thinks of you?
Every private thought. The ones they would never, ever say to your face.
Be honest. A part of you has always wanted to know. And a part of you is terrified to.
Because somewhere deep down, you have always quietly assumed the worst.
So you step out into the world, and you brace yourself for the noise.
And the thoughts come flooding in. A hundred quiet voices, all at once.
You flinch, waiting for the judgment you are so certain is coming.
The coworker you're sure resents you is quietly wishing he had your calm.
Wait. That isn't what you expected at all. Not even close.
The friend you snapped at last week forgot it by lunch. She's just glad you called.
That clumsy thing you said in the meeting, the one you still replay at three a.m.?
No one is thinking about it. No one else even remembers that it happened.
People think about you far, far less than you fear that they do.
Everyone is the nervous main character of their own private show.
That harsh, crowded audience you've been performing for your entire life...
was never really watching. And something you've carried for years gets lighter.
Then the volume shifts, and the quieter voices start to come through.
Your mother, across the city, thinking of you mid-sentence, for no reason at all.
An old friend, miles away. I hope they know I still think about them.
The people who love you think of you more, and far more gently, than you let yourself believe.
A stranger you helped once, years ago, who has never forgotten your face.
You spent so long bracing for the hate. You never once planned for this.
And then come the thoughts that ache.
Someone who needed you to ask if they were okay. And you never even noticed.
A quiet I miss you, from someone you slowly let drift away.
And the silence where certain voices used to be. The ones you can't hear anymore.
You would give anything for just one more of their thoughts.
But the loudest voice of all isn't a stranger's. It isn't even theirs.
It's the one that has been narrating your every flaw from the inside.
The cruelest critic you will ever meet has been wearing your face the whole time.
Then the sun goes down, the voices fade, and the day is finally over.
You can't really hear their thoughts. You never could. But maybe you don't need to.
Maybe you just stop assuming the worst, ask how they really are, and say the kind thing out loud.
Because everyone around you is guessing too. Bracing themselves, exactly like you were.
So whose thought would you most want to hear? Tell me below, and I'll see you in the next one.
